course_name_original: Análisis Dinámico y Modelado de Máquinas de Alterna
course_name_en: Dynamic Analysis and Modeling of AC Machines
prerequisites: It is highly recommended to keep the schedule of this course as it appears in the programme guide verification report). Particularly, the course should be taken before "Dynamic Control of AC Machines".

learning_outcomes.text: Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Knowledge of the principal mathematic tools used in the analysis, modeling and simulation of power systems.
Use of computers and digital processors in the analysis, design, simulation, monitoring, control and supervision of power systems.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical matters.
Characterization and modeling of the main energy sources and electric power loads.
Ability to understand the basics of the dynamic modeling of electrical power systems.
Electric machines in steady state and transient operation used for generation and traction
Ability to analyze and understand the design of electric drives.
Understanding the mathematical modeling of three-phase systems, particularly in AC machines.
Understanding the dq theory for modeling and analysis phase systems.
To analyze the dynamic behavior of AC machines according to the theory dq.
Analyzing the dynamic model of AC machines using equivalent circuits.

syllabus_topics: Stationary abc coordinate equations of three phase systems.
Representation of complex variables and three phase systems.
Modeling and analysis of the induction machine in dq coordinates.
Modeling and analysis of the synchronous machine in dq coordinates
Model of the induction machine in rotor flux oriented reference frame
Model of the permanent magnet machine in rotor reference frame
assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call is calculated as: Final Grade = (0.40 × EX) + (0.50 × HW) + (0.10 × AT). A minimum score of 4/10 is required for the Final Written Exam (EX) and Homework / Laboratory Work (HW); if this minimum is not met for either, the final grade for the ordinary call will be capped at 4.0. All homework/lab tasks must be submitted to pass the subject. The extraordinary call follows the same structure, weighting, and minimum requirements as the ordinary call.
bibliography: D. W. Novotny y T. A. Lipo, Vector Control and Dynamics of AC Drives. Oxford University Press, USA, 1996.
